stem: Which locations in Windows 10 and Windows 11 provide access to the Internet Properties system utility? (Select 3 answers)
explanation: Internet Properties opens from the Internet Options applet, from the Network and Sharing Center, and by running inetcpl.cpl.
options: Internet Options applet in Windows Control Panel
Network and Sharing Center applet in Windows Control Panel
Ease of Access applet in Windows Control Panel
Windows Run dialog box (after typing inetcpl.cpl, and pressing Enter)
Internet Options menu item in Microsoft Edge Tools menu
correctAnswer: Internet Options applet in Windows Control Panel
Network and Sharing Center applet in Windows Control Panel
Windows Run dialog box (after typing inetcpl.cpl, and pressing Enter)

stem: Which tab of the Windows Internet Properties applet provides an option for deleting temporary Internet files, cookies, web browsing and download history, saved passwords, and data typed into web forms?
explanation: The General tab holds the browsing history section, which deletes temporary files, cookies, history, passwords and form data.

stem: The Security tab of the Internet Properties applet in MS Windows allows users to configure zone-based restrictions for websites and control the type of content that can be accessed through the system's built-in web components.
explanation: True. The Security tab configures security zones (Internet, Local intranet, Trusted sites, Restricted sites).

stem: Which of the answers listed below refers to a Windows Internet Properties applet tab that provides settings for a built-in pop-up blocker?
explanation: The Privacy tab holds the pop-up blocker settings.

stem: Which tab of the Internet Properties applet in Windows provides access to advanced cookie management options?
explanation: Cookie handling is managed on the Privacy tab.

stem: Which of the Windows Internet Properties applet tabs enables the management of digital certificates, the AutoComplete functionality, and RSS feeds?
explanation: The Content tab handles certificates, AutoComplete and feeds.

stem: Which of the following answers refer to network settings accessible through the Connections tab of the Internet Properties applet in Windows? (Select 3 answers)
explanation: The Connections tab holds LAN settings, dial-up and VPN settings, and proxy server settings.

stem: Which of the Windows Internet Properties applet tabs provides options for managing web browser extensions and setting default applications?
explanation: The Programs tab manages add-ons and default programs.

stem: Which tab of the Windows Internet Properties applet provides access to detailed settings for customizing the built-in web browser's behavior, including options for resetting browser configurations, managing accessibility, browsing, security, and multimedia features?
explanation: The Advanced tab holds the detailed settings and the Reset option.

stem: Which of the answers listed below refer to features of the Windows Devices and Printers Control Panel applet? (Select 3 answers)
explanation: Devices and Printers gives a simplified view of connected devices and lets you add/remove them and troubleshoot. Driver rollback and the detailed view belong to Device Manager.
options: Allows users to add/remove wired and wireless devices
Provides a simplified view of all connected devices
Allows users to restore a device driver to the previously installed version
Provides a detailed view of all connected devices
Allows users to troubleshoot a device that is not working properly
correctAnswer: Allows users to add/remove wired and wireless devices
Provides a simplified view of all connected devices
Allows users to troubleshoot a device that is not working properly

stem: The Programs and Features Control Panel applet in Windows enables: (Select all that apply)
explanation: Programs and Features can repair or uninstall programs, turn Windows features on or off, and show installed updates. Restore points are in System Protection.
options: Accessing an option for enabling or disabling Windows features
Creating or deleting system restore points
Accessing an option to view installed updates
correctAnswer: Accessing an option for enabling or disabling Windows features
Accessing an option to view installed updates

stem: The Network and Sharing Center Control Panel applet in Windows allows users to: (Select 3 answers)
explanation: The Network and Sharing Center shows active networks, sets up new connections and troubleshoots network problems. Firewall and proxy settings are elsewhere.
options: Set up a new connection or network
correctAnswer: Set up a new connection or network

stem: The Network and Sharing Center Control Panel applet in Windows provides access to: (Select 3 answers)
explanation: It links to adapter settings, advanced sharing settings and media streaming options. Security zones are in Internet Properties.

stem: In newer versions of Microsoft Windows, the classic System applet in Control Panel has been deprecated and now redirects to the About page within the System section of the Settings app. The About page displays detailed hardware and system information, including CPU model and speed, installed and usable RAM, as well as the Windows edition and version. It also offers quick access to common system utilities such as Device Manager and System Properties. In premium editions of Windows 10 and 11, this page additionally includes links to BitLocker and Remote Desktop.
explanation: True. The classic System applet now redirects to Settings > System > About.

stem: In Windows 10 and 11, the About page within the System section of Windows Settings can be accessed through the following paths: (Select all that apply)
explanation: The About page can be reached from Control Panel (either view), the right-click Start menu, or Settings > System > About. Programs and Features doesn't lead there.
options: Windows Start > System (via right-click on the Start button)
Windows Control Panel (category view) > System and Security > System
Windows Start > Settings > System > About page
Windows Control Panel > Programs and Features > System
correctAnswer: Windows Start > System (via right-click on the Start button)
Windows Control Panel (category view) > System and Security > System
Windows Start > Settings > System > About page

stem: Which of the following Control Panel applets in Windows 10 and Windows 11 provides access to firewall settings?
explanation: The applet is called Windows Defender Firewall in Windows 10 and 11.

stem: In Windows 10 and Windows 11, the Control Panel applet providing access to Microsoft Outlook configuration options is called:
explanation: The Mail applet configures Outlook mail profiles and accounts.

stem: Which of the answers listed below refers to an audio configuration Control Panel applet in Windows 10 and Windows 11?
explanation: The Sound applet configures audio devices.

stem: Which applet in the Windows Control Panel enables the modification of local user account settings?
explanation: The User Accounts applet modifies local user account settings.

stem: Which Windows Control Panel applet allows users to manage hardware and driver settings?
explanation: Device Manager manages hardware and drivers (update, disable, roll back).

stem: A Windows Control Panel applet designed to improve file search performance is known as:
explanation: Indexing Options controls the search index, which speeds up file searches.

stem: Windows Administrative Tools (renamed to Windows Tools in Windows 11) is a folder within the Control Panel that serves as a centralized collection of shortcuts to various system utilities and management consoles primarily designed for advanced configuration, monitoring, troubleshooting, and maintenance tasks on a Windows computer.
explanation: True. Administrative Tools (Windows Tools in Windows 11) collects shortcuts to management consoles.

stem: Which path in the Windows 10 and Windows 11 Control Panel provides access to a configuration setting that enables displaying hidden files, folders, and drives?
explanation: The path is File Explorer Options > View tab > Advanced settings > Show hidden files, folders, and drives.
options: Folder Options applet > General tab > Show hidden files, folders, and drives
File Explorer Options applet > View tab > Advanced settings: > Show hidden files, folders, and drives
Folder Options applet > General tab > Advanced settings: > Show hidden files, folders, and drives
File Explorer Options applet > Advanced settings: > Show hidden files, folders, and drives
correctAnswer: File Explorer Options applet > View tab > Advanced settings: > Show hidden files, folders, and drives

stem: Which of the following actions provides access to the Windows 10 and Windows 11 File Explorer setting that toggles the visibility of files and folders marked by default as hidden?
explanation: In File Explorer (Windows key + E), the View menu has a Hidden items checkbox.
options: Windows logo key + E > View > Hidden items
Windows logo key + F > File > Change folder and search options > Hidden items
Windows logo key + E > View > Advanced settings > Hidden items
Windows logo key + F > File > Show hidden files and folders
correctAnswer: Windows logo key + E > View > Hidden items

stem: Which sequence of steps in Windows 10 and Windows 11 Control Panel provides access to a configuration setting that enables showing or hiding extensions for known file types?
explanation: The setting is under File Explorer Options > View tab > Advanced settings > Hide extensions for known file types.
options: Folder Options applet > View tab > Hide extensions for known file types
File Explorer Options applet > View tab > Advanced settings: > Hide extensions for known file types
Folder Options applet > General tab > Hide extensions for known file types
File Explorer Options applet > Advanced settings tab > Hide extensions for known file types
correctAnswer: File Explorer Options applet > View tab > Advanced settings: > Hide extensions for known file types

stem: The File Explorer setting that enables showing or hiding extensions for known file types in Windows 10 and 11 can be accessed via:
explanation: In File Explorer, View has a File name extensions checkbox for quick toggling.
options: Windows logo key + E > View > File name extensions
Windows logo key + F > File > Change folder and search options > File name extensions
Windows logo key + E > View > Options > Advanced settings > File name extensions
Windows logo key + F > File > Settings > File name extensions
correctAnswer: Windows logo key + E > View > File name extensions

stem: Which of the settings listed below is not part of the General tab of the File Explorer Options Control Panel applet in Windows 10 and Windows 11?
explanation: Hidden file visibility is on the View tab. The General tab covers the starting folder, browsing, opening items and privacy/history.
options: Selection of the default starting folder after launching File Explorer
Visibility of hidden files, folders, and drives
Folder browsing options (opening each folder in the same window or in its own window)
Opening items (single-click vs. double-click to open an item)
File Explorer browsing history options (Privacy section)
correctAnswer: Visibility of hidden files, folders, and drives

stem: In Windows 10 and Windows 11, the File Explorer View menu (accessed via Windows logo key + E > View) enables quick visual and layout changes for the current folder, while the File Explorer Options View tab (accessed via Control Panel > File Explorer Options > View) provides access to a system-wide, persistent configuration interface for File Explorer behavior.
explanation: True. The View menu is for quick changes. The Options dialog holds system-wide settings.

stem: Which of the following answers refer to hibernation mode in Windows? (Select 3 answers)
explanation: Hibernation saves the system state to disk and powers off, so it uses no power and resumes more slowly than sleep.
options: Saves the system state (e.g., all open/unsaved files and running applications) to a storage drive
Resumes full system operation more slowly than it does when waking from sleep mode
Turns the computer off after saving the system state to disk
Requires a small amount of power to maintain system memory
Keeps system state (e.g., all open/unsaved files and running applications) in RAM
Resumes full system operation faster than when waking from sleep mode
correctAnswer: Saves the system state (e.g., all open/unsaved files and running applications) to a storage drive
Resumes full system operation more slowly than it does when waking from sleep mode
Turns the computer off after saving the system state to disk

stem: A Windows power plan is a collection of hardware and system settings that determine how the computer uses power. In Windows Control Panel, the applet providing access to these settings is called:
explanation: Power Options is the applet for power plans.

stem: Which of the statements listed below describe the behavior of sleep mode in Windows? (Select 3 answers)
explanation: Sleep keeps the state in RAM, uses a small amount of power and resumes faster than hibernation.
options: Requires a small amount of power to maintain system memory
Saves the system state (e.g., all open/unsaved files and running applications) to a storage drive
Turns the computer off after saving the system state to disk
Resumes full system operation faster than it does when recovering from hibernation mode
Keeps the system state (e.g., all open/unsaved files and running applications) in RAM
Resumes full system operation more slowly than when recovering from hibernation mode
correctAnswer: Requires a small amount of power to maintain system memory
Resumes full system operation faster than it does when recovering from hibernation mode
Keeps the system state (e.g., all open/unsaved files and running applications) in RAM

stem: On Windows-based laptops, the Microsoft operating system includes an additional power configuration setting that lets users choose what happens when the laptop lid is closed (e.g., Do Nothing, Sleep, Hibernate, or Shutdown). This setting can be accessed via the following steps: (Select all that apply)
explanation: Choose what closing the lid does is under Power Options, reached from Control Panel (either view) or Settings > System > Power & sleep. Power & sleep is not under Devices.
options: Windows Control Panel (category view) > Hardware and Sound > Power Options > Choose what closing the lid does
Windows Start > Settings > System > Power & sleep > Additional power settings > Choose what closing the lid does
Windows Control Panel (icon view) > Power Options > Choose what closing the lid does
Windows Start > Settings > Devices > Power & sleep > Additional power settings > Choose what closing the lid does
correctAnswer: Windows Control Panel (category view) > Hardware and Sound > Power Options > Choose what closing the lid does
Windows Start > Settings > System > Power & sleep > Additional power settings > Choose what closing the lid does
Windows Control Panel (icon view) > Power Options > Choose what closing the lid does

stem: The fast startup feature in Windows 10 and 11 puts the computer into a hibernation-like state, allowing the system to resume operation more quickly when powered on. Which of the actions listed below provide(s) access to this setting? (Select all that apply)
explanation: Fast startup is under Power Options > Choose what the power buttons do > Change settings that are currently unavailable. Settings > Devices isn't a valid route.
options: Windows Control Panel (category view) > Hardware and Sound > Power Options > Choose what the power buttons do > Change settings that are currently unavailable > Turn on fast startup
Windows Start > Settings > Devices > Power & sleep > Additional power settings > Choose what the power buttons do > Change settings that are currently unavailable > Turn on fast startup
Windows Control Panel (icon view) > Power Options > Choose what the power buttons do > Change settings that are currently unavailable > Turn on fast startup
Windows Start > Settings > System > Power & sleep > Additional power settings > Choose what the power buttons do > Change settings that are currently unavailable > Turn on fast startup
correctAnswer: Windows Control Panel (category view) > Hardware and Sound > Power Options > Choose what the power buttons do > Change settings that are currently unavailable > Turn on fast startup
Windows Control Panel (icon view) > Power Options > Choose what the power buttons do > Change settings that are currently unavailable > Turn on fast startup
Windows Start > Settings > System > Power & sleep > Additional power settings > Choose what the power buttons do > Change settings that are currently unavailable > Turn on fast startup

stem: USB selective suspend is a power-saving feature in Windows that allows the system to temporarily disable an individual USB port when the connected device is not in use. The USB selective suspend setting can be accessed via: (Select all that apply)
explanation: USB selective suspend is in a power plan's advanced settings under USB settings. The routes through Control Panel and Settings > System lead there, and Settings > Devices doesn't.
options: Windows Control Panel (icon view) > Power Options > Change plan settings > Change advanced power settings > USB settings > USB selective suspend setting
Windows Start > Settings > System > Power & sleep > Additional power settings > Change plan settings > Change advanced power settings > USB settings > USB selective suspend setting
Windows Control Panel (category view) > Hardware and Sound > Power Options > Change plan settings > Change advanced power settings > USB settings > USB selective suspend setting
Windows Start > Settings > Devices > Power & sleep > Additional power settings > Change plan settings > Change advanced power settings > USB settings > USB selective suspend setting
correctAnswer: Windows Control Panel (icon view) > Power Options > Change plan settings > Change advanced power settings > USB settings > USB selective suspend setting
Windows Start > Settings > System > Power & sleep > Additional power settings > Change plan settings > Change advanced power settings > USB settings > USB selective suspend setting
Windows Control Panel (category view) > Hardware and Sound > Power Options > Change plan settings > Change advanced power settings > USB settings > USB selective suspend setting

stem: Which of the following sections of the Settings app in Windows 10 includes configuration options aimed at users with disabilities?
explanation: Ease of Access is the Windows 10 Settings section for accessibility options.

stem: Which section of the Windows Settings app enables configuration of date, time, region, language, and speech recognition settings?
explanation: Time & Language holds date, time, region, language and speech settings.

stem: Which of the sections listed below provides access to backup, recovery, and OS upgrade options within the Windows 10 Settings app?
explanation: Windows 10's Update & Security section covers updates, backup, recovery and activation.

stem: In the Windows Settings app, which section hosts desktop customization settings?
explanation: Personalization holds desktop customization such as background, colors and themes.

stem: Which section of the Windows Settings app includes options to modify installed programs?
explanation: The Apps section lets you modify or uninstall installed programs.

stem: Which section of the Settings app in Windows 10 allows users to modify permissions for the operating system and applications?
explanation: Privacy controls permissions for the OS and apps. Privacy & security is the Windows 11 name.

stem: In the Windows Settings app, which section provides access to settings for display, sound, notifications, power management, and storage?
explanation: The System section holds display, sound, notifications, power and storage settings.

stem: Which section of the Settings app in Windows 10 includes options for managing Bluetooth devices, printers, and other connected hardware?
explanation: In Windows 10, Settings > Devices manages Bluetooth devices, printers and connected hardware. Bluetooth & devices is the Windows 11 name.

stem: Which section of the Windows Settings app provides access to network configuration options?
explanation: Network & Internet is the Settings section for network configuration.

stem: Which of the following enables access to gaming options in the Windows Settings app?
explanation: The Gaming section holds Game bar, captures and Game Mode.

stem: Which section of the Settings app in Windows 10 and Windows 11 allows users to manage sign-in options and connected account settings, including email?
explanation: The Accounts section manages sign-in options and account settings, including email accounts.
